title: Chocolate bar fractions
concept: Comparing fractions with different denominators: 5/9 vs 4/7. A bigger top and bottom number does not mean a bigger amount, because the bottom number sets the piece size. 4/7 is bigger: 36/63 vs 35/63.
kept: The question: which is bigger, 5/9 or 4/7
Two chocolate bars of the same size, one cut into 9 pieces and one into 7
Taking 5 and 4 pieces and putting them next to each other to compare
Order: guess which is bigger, then cut the bars, then compare, then try other fractions
The student's common-denominator method (5/9 = 35/63, 4/7 = 36/63) and the decimal method, both shown in the explanation
The friend's likely mistake (5 and 9 are bigger numbers) named in the guess feedback
Chocolate, cozy look: dark and milk chocolate bars, warm cream background, serif title
filled_in: Cutting is done with one button per bar; taking is done by tapping pieces, which move into two rows lined up from the same left edge
Dashed orange markers at the end of each row so the small gap (1/63 of a bar) is visible

A 'Cut into tiny matching pieces' button that draws the common-denominator grid (63 tiny pieces) on the bars and rows so the visitor can count 35 vs 36; this is the student's own common-denominator idea made visible, not a new activity
'Try other fractions' as four sliders (pieces each bar is cut into, 2-12; pieces taken, up to that number)
Plain-word definitions of fraction, numerator, denominator and common denominator; 'of a bar' as the unit
Takeaway sentence in the card once the visitor explores
Model footer noting that the pieces are perfectly equal, unlike real chocolate
math_check: Design math is correct (5/9 = 35/63 < 36/63 = 4/7). All numbers are computed in code: pieces taken are counted from the visitor's taps; fractions and the difference use MK.frac (5/9 vs 4/7 gives 4/7 bigger by 1/63); tiny-piece counts use lcm(9,7) = 63 and n x (63/d) = 35 and 36; decimals are n/d to 3 places (0.556, 0.571). Walked through in a headless browser and recomputed by hand: 5/9 vs 4/7 -> 35/63 vs 36/63, difference 1/63; 2/3 vs 3/5 -> 10/15 vs 9/15, difference 1/15; 12/12 vs 12/12 -> same amount. check-page.mjs passes with no problems or warnings.
